module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 213

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/213](https://www.erdosproblems.com/213)
-/

@[expose] public section

open EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos213

/--
The predicate (on $n$) that there exist $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$,
no three on a line and no four on a circle,
such that all pairwise distances are integers.
-/
def Erdos213For (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ S : Set ℝ², S.Finite ∧ S.ncard = n ∧
    NonTrilinear S ∧
    (∀ Q : Set ℝ², Q ⊆ S ∧ Q.ncard = 4 → ¬ EuclideanGeometry.Cospherical Q) ∧
    (S.Pairwise fun p₁ p₂ => dist p₁ p₂ ∈ Set.range Int.cast)

/--
Let $n \geq 4$. Are there $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line and no four on a circle,
such that all pairwise distances are integers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_213 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 4 → Erdos213For n := by sorry

/--
The best construction to date, due to Kreisel and Kurz, has $n = 7$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_213.variants.KK08 : Erdos213For 7 := by sorry

end Erdos213

review.notes: All three declarations were checked and match the sources. The source asks the question for every n ≥ 4, still labels it OPEN, and records the Kreisel–Kurz seven-point construction, agreeing with both theorem categories. Lean proofs in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verify that NonTrilinear tests distinct triples, four-point cardinality excludes infinite sets, Cospherical necessarily has positive radius on four points, and integer distances between distinct points are positive integers. Exact computations in /workspace/review/computation.lean also verified a four-point boundary example and the distances and general-position determinants of the paper's seven-point coordinates. No mathematical or status defects found.
